name: England & Wales
jurisdiction: England (Tenant Fees Act 2019) and Wales (Renting Homes (Fees etc.) (Wales) Act 2019)
summary: Assured shorthold and similar private tenancies. Most tenant fees are banned and deposits are capped. Renting reforms are in progress in England; check gov.uk for what is in force on your signing date.

rules.title: Fee that may be a prohibited payment
rules.note: In England, the Tenant Fees Act 2019 bans most fees beyond rent, a capped refundable deposit, a holding deposit, and a short list of permitted payments (for example utilities, council tax, certain default fees, and up to GBP 50 for agreed changes to the tenancy). Wales has a similar Act.
rules.ask: Which permitted payment under the Tenant Fees Act 2019 does this fee fall under?
rules.source: Tenant Fees Act 2019, Schedule 1 (legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2019/4); Renting Homes (Fees etc.) (Wales) Act 2019.

rules.title: Deposit above the 5-week cap
rules.note: Under the Tenant Fees Act 2019 a tenancy deposit is generally capped at 5 weeks' rent where annual rent is under GBP 50,000 (6 weeks at or above that).
rules.ask: The deposit looks higher than 5 weeks' rent. Can it be reduced to the cap, and which protection scheme will hold it?
rules.green: The deposit appears to be within the 5-week cap.

rules.title: Late rent charges before 14 days
rules.note: A default fee for late rent is generally only permitted once rent is at least 14 days overdue, and is limited to interest at no more than 3% above the Bank of England base rate.
rules.ask: Can the late rent clause follow the Tenant Fees Act limits (14 days, interest at 3% above base rate)?
rules.green: Late charges only start after 14 days.

rules.title: Flat late fee
rules.note: A flat late fee, rather than interest on the overdue amount, may not fit the permitted default payment for late rent.
rules.ask: Can the flat late fee be replaced by interest capped at 3% above the Bank of England base rate?

rules.title: Renewal and rollover terms
rules.note: Rollover terms and fixed-term structures are changing under renting reform in England. Make sure you understand what happens at the end of the term and how much notice you must give.
rules.ask: What happens at the end of the term, and what notice do I need to give to leave?
rules.source: gov.uk guidance on private renting (check current status).

rules.title: Long tenant notice period
rules.note: One month (or one rental period) is common for tenants in periodic tenancies. Longer notice terms are worth checking.
rules.ask: Can the tenant notice period be one month?
rules.green: Tenant notice is within a common range.

rules.title: Early termination charge
rules.note: A payment for leaving early at your request is permitted, but generally should not exceed the landlord's actual loss or reasonable costs.
rules.ask: How is the early termination charge calculated, and will it be limited to your reasonable costs?

rules.title: Repairs pushed onto the tenant
rules.note: Landlords generally keep repair duties for structure, exterior, and installations for water, gas, electricity, heating and sanitation, and these cannot usually be contracted out.
rules.ask: Will you confirm that structural, heating, plumbing and electrical repairs remain the landlord's responsibility?
